title: The Art of Thinking in a Digital World
abstract: Luc de Brabandere has had three careers in his fifty years of professional life. He started out as a computer engineer, before becoming a consultant in creativity, and today he is a corporate philosopher. This journey has led him to investigate successively the three modes of thinking that are permanently articulated within us: logical thinking, creative thinking and critical thinking. As a talented popularizer, he puts forward an ambitious yet accessible summary of the main principles that govern these three modes of thinking. The book is richly illustrated and places thinking in an historical perspective that allows us to better understand how informational technology in general, and ChatGPT and other artificial intelligences in particular, are influencing our mental models. In the first part of this book, thinking is presented as a game whose rules need to be understood in order to be able to play the game better. A machine can’t be creative or responsible. So the more machines there are, the more thinking we’ll need to do!

Short impact summary

Published in 2024 by Peter Lang Verlag, Luc de Brabandere's The Art of Thinking in a Digital World presents a synthesis of logical, creative, and critical thinking across three decades of professional experience spanning computer engineering, creativity consulting, and corporate philosophy. The work has begun to reach academic and professional audiences through institutional adoption and recorded educational content, though formal citation activity remains in its early stages.

Full narrative

De Brabandere brings an unusual intellectual trajectory to this inquiry into human cognition in technological contexts. His progression from computer engineer to creativity consultant to corporate philosopher provides the experiential foundation for an accessible examination of three complementary modes of thought. The book positions itself as an ambitious yet readable overview of cognitive principles, bridging technical and humanistic perspectives on how minds engage with digital environments.

Early evidence of adoption appears within professional development contexts. The Institute for Management Development (IMD) has featured the work in recorded video content, suggesting uptake among practitioners and educators in executive education and organizational leadership. This channel of dissemination reflects the book's alignment with applied domains of management and thinking skills rather than purely academic ones.

The work is registered in library systems and institutional repositories, indicating accessibility through standard scholarly discovery pathways. Data citation pathways are active, showing that the underlying research infrastructure recognizes the work's standing as a citable resource. These early structural signals suggest the book is entering professional and educational circulation, though formal scholarly citation has not yet accumulated.

As a 2024 publication, the work is still establishing its presence in scholarly conversations. Its current profile is consistent with a newly released title building readership through institutional channels and professional networks rather than through immediate academic citation. The strength of its reach at this stage lies in its adoption by educational organizations and its accessibility to non-specialist audiences seeking frameworks for thinking in digital contexts.
